content: Rifampin and isoniazid are indicated for the treatment of pulmonary tuberculosis caused by susceptible organisms. This fixed-dose combination is only recommended after the patient has been stabilized on the individual components and it has been confirmed that the fixed dosage is therapeutically effective. The standard dose is rifampin 600 mg and isoniazid 300 mg (two capsules) taken orally once daily. This combination is not recommended for initial tuberculosis therapy or for preventive therapy. Its safety and efficacy have not been established in patients under 15 years of age. Rifampin interacts with numerous drugs by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzymes, particularly CYP3A4, which can significantly alter the metabolism and efficacy of co-administered medications. Below are specific examples of these interactions: 1. Artemether/lumefantrine: Rifampin reduces their levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, leading to decreased antimalarial efficacy. Co-administration is contraindicated. 2. Atazanavir: Rifampin increases its metabolism, reducing antiviral efficacy and potentially leading to viral resistance. Co-administration is contraindicated. 3. Bictegravir: Rifampin decreases its plasma concentration by inducing CYP3A4 and UGT1A1 enzymes, risking therapeutic failure and resistance. Co-administration is contraindicated. 4. Cabotegravir: Co-administration is contraindicated. 5. Cariprazine: Rifampin reduces its levels by inducing CYP3A4, potentially diminishing therapeutic effects. Co-administration is contraindicated. 6. Cobicistat: Rifampin reduces its levels, risking loss of therapeutic effect and resistance. Co-administration is contraindicated. 7. Cobimetinib: Co-administration is contraindicated. 8. Darunavir: Rifampin increases its metabolism, leading to loss of antiviral efficacy and potential resistance. Co-administration is contraindicated. 9. Doravirine: Rifampin reduces its plasma concentrations, risking virologic failure and resistance. Co-administration is contraindicated. 10. Elbasvir/grazoprevir: Rifampin reduces their therapeutic effect by inducing CYP3A4. Co-administration is contraindicated. 11. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF: Rifampin reduces their levels, risking virologic failure and resistance. Co-administration is contraindicated. 12. Etravirine: Rifampin increases its metabolism, reducing efficacy. Co-administration is contraindicated. 13. Fosamprenavir: Rifampin increases its metabolism, risking loss of antiviral efficacy. Co-administration is contraindicated. 14. Fostemsavir: Rifampin significantly decreases its active metabolite levels, risking virologic failure. Co-administration is contraindicated. 15. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir: Rifampin reduces their plasma concentrations and therapeutic effect. Co-administration is contraindicated. 16. Irinotecan: Rifampin reduces its levels by inducing CYP2B6 metabolism, risking therapeutic failure. Co-administration is contraindicated. 17. Isavuconazonium sulfate: Rifampin reduces its levels, risking therapeutic failure. Co-administration is contraindicated. 18. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir: Rifampin reduces sofosbuvir's active metabolite levels, risking therapeutic failure. Co-administration is contraindicated. 19. Lenacapavir: Rifampin reduces its levels, risking therapeutic failure. Co-administration is contraindicated. 20. Lopinavir/ritonavir: Rifampin reduces their levels, risking virologic failure. Co-administration is contraindicated. 21. Lurasidone: Rifampin reduces its levels, risking therapeutic failure. Co-administration is contraindicated. 22. Mavacamten: Rifampin reduces its levels by inducing CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism, risking therapeutic failure. Co-administration is contraindicated. 23. Naloxegol: Rifampin reduces its levels, risking therapeutic failure. Co-administration is not recommended. 24. Nelfinavir: Rifampin reduces its plasma concentrations, risking therapeutic failure and resistance. Co-administration is contraindicated. 25. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir: Rifampin reduces nirmatrelvir levels, risking virologic failure and resistance. Co-administration is contraindicated. 26. Ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir & dasabuvir: Rifampin reduces their levels, risking therapeutic failure. Co-administration is contraindicated. 27. Panobinostat: Rifampin reduces its levels by ~70%, risking treatment failure. Co-administration is contraindicated. 28. Pirfenidone: Rifampin reduces its levels, risking therapeutic failure. Co-administration is contraindicated. 29. Praziquantel: Rifampin reduces its levels, risking therapeutic failure. Co-administration is contraindicated. 30. Regorafenib: Co-administration is contraindicated. 31. Rilpivirine: Rifampin reduces its levels, risking virologic failure and resistance. Co-administration is contraindicated. 32. Roflumilast: Co-administration is not recommended. 33. Tipranavir: Rifampin reduces its levels, risking virologic failure and resistance. Co-administration is contraindicated. 34. Vandetanib: Co-administration is contraindicated. 35. Velpatasvir: Rifampin reduces its levels, risking therapeutic failure. Co-administration is contraindicated. 36. Voriconazole: Rifampin reduces its levels, risking therapeutic failure. Co-administration is contraindicated. For many other drugs, rifampin either reduces their plasma concentrations or increases their metabolism, leading to reduced efficacy or therapeutic failure. In such cases, co-administration is either contraindicated or requires careful consideration of alternative therapies or dose adjustments.
